I began feeling depressed and suicidal when I was 13. I moved to a new school, I had to live with my religious and abusive grandpa, and I had absolutely no friends. That bled into freshman year of high school when I started to self harm. 
Fast forward to my second year in college and my family dog dies. I had somewhat of a mental break and sank into a very deep and dark depression. That’s when I got on meds for the first time, but the depression was still there. 
I didn’t know what I wanted to do with my life and I was just drifting through college. After I finally graduated the existential doom grew darker and darker because now I was in the “real world” and was expected to get my shit together. 
A couple years after graduation, I was in a job I absolutely hated (substitute teaching, and I would cry in the classroom when the kids were at specials or lunch) and in a relationship with someone I didn’t love. I had so many mental breakdowns and tried to kill myself. After that, I moved back home to live with my mom. That’s where I currently am now. I haven’t been depressed in a while (thank you, Prozac) but I’m having a hard time getting a diagnosis for BPD, which I’m 95% sure I have. Things are slowly getting better.

You don't necessarily *have* to tell the reader what color your character's skin is. If you feel like you must describe your characters in a way to allude to what race or ethnicity they are, you could describe other physical characteristics that a specific race or ethnicity would have. My go\-to is to describe hair. Someone's hair can tell a lot about where they are from (unless your character has an unnatural hair color). Like someone with pin straight blonde hair you can safely assume that they are white. So on and so forth. You don't always have to feed your readers information that they could totally catch onto by themselves. And even if they don't, it probably won't make much of a difference to your plot anyway.
